section_summary: This section documents diplomatic, administrative, and technical matters concerning shortwave radio broadcasting and reception across the Pacific between December 1940 and January 1942. It covers the resolution of Columbia Broadcasting System's broadcasting suspension in Japan, extensive monitoring and technical coordination by the State Department, FCC, and General Electric regarding KGEI broadcast reception and interference in Chungking and Shanghai, and political analyses of Chinese broadcasts. It concludes with FBI transmittals of translated Tokyo radio broadcasts from late 1941, detailing deteriorating US-Japanese relations and Japan's Imperial declaration of war on December 8, 1941.

subfiles.about: Enclosures to Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 5211 concerning the temporary broadcasting ban imposed on CBS in Japan and its resolution.
subfiles.summary: Enclosures transmit correspondence from CBS representative W. R. Wills and an oral statement presented by Ambassador Grew to the Japanese Foreign Minister. The documents address allegations that CBS broadcast remarks disparaging to Japan, concluding with assurances that broadcasting arrangements would be restored.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5211 (Enclosures): Debarment of Columbia Broadcasting System from Broadcasting from Japan

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of a Tokyo Embassy despatch concerning radio interference caused by Japanese station JZP to Press Wireless station JS.
subfiles.summary: FCC Chairman Fly acknowledges receipt of a Tokyo Embassy report on interference caused by Japanese station JZP to Press Wireless station JS.
subfiles.title: Letter from FCC Chairman Fly to Secretary of State regarding radio interference

subfiles.about: Reports severe interference and reception problems experienced by San Francisco station KGEI in Chungking and the Far East.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Johnson reports that KGEI's 31-meter band is crowded out by competing international broadcasts, urging KGEI to utilize less crowded frequencies.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 35 from Chungking regarding KGEI broadcast reception in the Far East

subfiles.about: Department of State paraphrase of Ambassador Johnson's telegram concerning KGEI shortwave broadcast reception difficulties in China.
subfiles.summary: State Department paraphrase of the January 20 telegram from Chungking reporting heavy interference and reception difficulties for station KGEI.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Telegram No. 35 from Chungking regarding KGEI reception

subfiles.about: Transmits for comment a paraphrase of the Chungking Embassy telegram regarding reception of station KGEI.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the FCC Chairman a paraphrase of the Chungking telegram concerning Far Eastern reception of KGEI.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to FCC Chairman transmitting Chungking telegram paraphrase

subfiles.about: Transmits a paraphrase of the Chungking Embassy telegram concerning KGEI broadcast reception for General Electric's information and comment.
subfiles.summary: Thomas Burke transmits to General Electric a paraphrase of the January 20 Chungking telegram regarding Far Eastern reception of KGEI broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to General Electric Company transmitting Chungking telegram paraphrase

subfiles.about: Relays FCC information regarding KGEI frequency assignments and requests reception monitoring data on 9670 kc.
subfiles.summary: The State Department relays FCC statements explaining frequency assignments for station KGEI and requests Chungking report whether reception on 9670 kc experiences interference.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 34 to Chungking regarding KGEI frequency assignments and interference

subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of State Department letter transmitting the Chungking telegram paraphrase concerning KGEI.
subfiles.summary: General Electric acknowledges receipt of the State Department's communication enclosing the paraphrase of the Chungking telegram regarding KGEI reception.
subfiles.title: Letter from General Electric Company acknowledging State Department communication on KGEI

subfiles.about: Discusses propagation characteristics of KGEI frequencies and requests reports on whether 9670 kc suffers objectionable interference.
subfiles.summary: FCC Chairman Fly outlines frequency assignments for station KGEI broadcasts to Asia and asks if broadcasts on 9670 kc encounter interference.
subfiles.title: Letter from FCC Chairman Fly to Secretary of State regarding KGEI frequencies

subfiles.about: Informs the FCC that its inquiry concerning KGEI reception has been telegraphed to the American Embassy in Chungking.
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary Long informs FCC Chairman Fly that the Commission's inquiry regarding KGEI interference was cabled to the American Embassy at Chungking.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary Long to FCC Chairman Fly regarding KGEI inquiry

subfiles.about: Provides daily monitoring logs of KGEI reception on 9670 kc at Chungking between February 20 and 26, 1941.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Johnson submits reception log entries for station KGEI on 9670 kc in Chungking, noting deliberate interference and comparing shortwave wavebands.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 44 from Chungking reporting on KGEI reception

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of Chungking Embassy's March 3 telegram reporting on KGEI reception.
subfiles.summary: Assistant Secretary Long transmits to FCC Chairman Fly copies of the Chungking Embassy's March 3 telegram reporting on KGEI reception.
subfiles.title: Letter from Assistant Secretary Long to FCC Chairman Fly transmitting Chungking reception report

subfiles.about: Summarizes reception conditions of KGEI broadcasts on 9670 kc and 15330 kc in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Lockhart reports on Shanghai reception of station KGEI, highlighting listener interest in news and requesting slower delivery of announcements.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Shanghai reporting on KGEI reception

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of Shanghai Consulate General's March 12 telegram regarding KGEI reception.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the FCC Chairman a copy of the March 12 telegram from Shanghai regarding KGEI reception.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to FCC Chairman transmitting Shanghai telegram

subfiles.about: Reports clear Shanghai reception of President Roosevelt's March 14 address over KGEI and its local rebroadcast.
subfiles.summary: Consul General Lockhart reports excellent reception in Shanghai of President Roosevelt's address over KGEI and its longwave rebroadcast by station XMHC.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 299 from Shanghai regarding reception of President Roosevelt's address

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of Shanghai telegram No. 299 regarding reception of President Roosevelt's address.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the FCC Chairman a copy of Shanghai telegram No. 299 concerning KGEI reception of Roosevelt's speech.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to FCC Chairman transmitting Shanghai telegram No. 299

subfiles.about: Transmits a copy of Shanghai telegram No. 299 concerning KGEI reception of President Roosevelt's speech to General Electric.
subfiles.summary: Thomas Burke transmits to Robert S. Peare of General Electric a copy of the March 17 telegram from Shanghai regarding KGEI reception.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to General Electric Company transmitting Shanghai telegram No. 299

subfiles.about: Details Shanghai reception of President Roosevelt's White House Correspondents' Dinner address broadcast over KGEI and its rebroadcast by station XMHC.
subfiles.summary: Consul A. Viola Smith reports on Shanghai reception of President Roosevelt's address over KGEI, its rebroadcast over longwave by station XMHC arranged through engineer I. L. Lowe, local press reactions, and reception of an NBC symphony concert.
subfiles.title: Report from Shanghai on KGEI reception: President Roosevelt's Address

subfiles.about: Comprehensive report and technical listener logs assessing shortwave broadcasts from station KGEI received in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: Consul A. Viola Smith compiles a comprehensive study on shortwave reception of station KGEI in Shanghai, reviewing program popularity, waveband congestion, and atmospheric interference. Appended enclosures provide detailed listening logs and receiver specifications from local residents Victor Hanson, G. Swan, and XMHC engineer I. L. Lowe.
subfiles.title: Required Report: Short Wave Broadcasts from the United States – Shanghai Reception of KGEI

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of two Shanghai consular reports regarding reception of station KGEI shortwave broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: Thomas Burke transmits to Robert S. Peare of General Electric copies of consular reports from Shanghai dated March 11 and March 18 regarding KGEI reception.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of State to General Electric Company transmitting Shanghai consular reports

subfiles.about: Transmits copies of two Shanghai consular reports regarding reception of station KGEI broadcasts.
subfiles.summary: The Secretary of State transmits to the FCC Chairman copies of consular reports from Shanghai concerning reception of KGEI broadcasts.
subfiles.title: Note from Secretary of State to FCC Chairman transmitting Shanghai consular reports

subfiles.about: Transmits General Electric's technical commentary and explanations regarding KGEI shortwave broadcast reception and programming in Shanghai.
subfiles.summary: The Department of Commerce transmits General Electric's technical reply regarding KGEI reception in Shanghai, addressing German co-channel interference on 9675 kc, transmitter improvements, seasonal propagation across the Pacific, and slowing message delivery on the Missionary Mail Bag program.
subfiles.title: Letter from Department of Commerce transmitting General Electric comments on KGEI reception

subfiles.about: Provides excerpts from monitored Chungking broadcasts analyzing Japanese political changes, cabinet politics, and international relations.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum quoting excerpts from Chinese broadcasts over station XGOY in Chungking, analyzing Prince Konoye's cabinet, rising American hostility toward Japan, British economic embargoes, and the Anglo-Soviet pact.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for Mr. Hornbeck: Transcripts of Chungking Broadcasts (Station XGOY)

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet noting the transfer of document 894.74/277 to file 811.74 Short Wave.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference sheet recording the transfer of decimal document 894.74/277 to file 811.74 Short Wave.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Document 894.74/277 transfer

subfiles.about: Transmits translated monitoring transcripts of Station JZI Tokyo radio broadcasts from late November and December 1941, including Japan's declaration of war.
subfiles.summary: FBI Director Hoover transmits translated monitoring transcripts of Radio Tokyo broadcasts. Broadcasts from November 27 detail Japanese assessments of the Washington diplomatic negotiations, alleged ABCD encirclement, and commentary on the Anti-Comintern Pact. Broadcasts from December 8 announce the Imperial declaration of war against the United States and Great Britain, widespread attacks across the Pacific, emergency cabinet actions, and appeals for national unity.
subfiles.title: Letter from FBI Director Hoover transmitting translated transcripts of Tokyo radio broadcasts
